collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IV: ROMANCE, COURTSHIP AND WEDDINGS (LCD-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Crushes and courting on Isola: wondering whether someone likes you back, flowers and love songs, first dates, serenades gone wrong, proposals, weddings big and small, how many children, breakups and starting over.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager plans to serenade their love under the window at night: sing it, or ask the drummers to help.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has decided to serenade (friend), the old way: at night, outside (friend.his/her) hut, with a song (subject.he/she) wrote (subject.him/her)self. The trouble is that (friend) shares the hut with (friend.his/her) grandmother, two cousins and a very loud dog. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) stands outside the hut under the moon and sings. The dog howls along. The cousins come out to watch. The grandmother shouts that some people are trying to sleep. (friend) comes out last, laughing so hard (friend.he/she) can barely stand, and sits down to hear the rest.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) brings three drummers and a flute player. It is far too loud. Half the village wakes up and comes to see. By the end of the song, there is a small crowd dancing outside (friend)'s hut, and (friend) is dancing with (subject) in the middle of it.
